concept: Linear Equation in 2 or more Variables
question: The system of equations: 2x + 3y = 7 and (a - b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b - 2 have infinitely many solutions:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For infinitely many solutions, the ratio of coefficients must be equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂.

⇒ 2 / (a − b) = 3 / (a + b)

⇒ 2a + 2b = 3a − 3b ⇒ a = 5b

Check options: Only Option 4 has a = 5 and b = 1, which perfectly satisfies a = 5b.

**∴ The correct answer is a = 5, b = 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

2x + 3y = 7

(a − b)x + (a + b)y = 3a + b − 2

**Formula Used:**

For a system of equations to have infinitely many solutions, the ratio of their coefficients must be equal:

a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Here, a₁ = 2, b₁ = 3, c₁ = 7

⇒ a₂ = (a − b), b₂ = (a + b), c₂ = (3a + b − 2)

⇒ 2 / (a − b) = 3 / (a + b) = 7 / (3a + b − 2)

⇒ Equating the first two parts:

⇒ 2 / (a − b) = 3 / (a + b)

⇒ 2(a + b) = 3(a − b)

⇒ 2a + 2b = 3a − 3b

⇒ a = 5b --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Equating the second and third parts:

⇒ 3 / (a + b) = 7 / (3a + b − 2)

⇒ 3(3a + b − 2) = 7(a + b)

⇒ 9a + 3b − 6 = 7a + 7b

⇒ 2a − 4b = 6

⇒ a − 2b = 3 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Substituting a = 5b into Equation 2:

⇒ 5b − 2b = 3

⇒ 3b = 3 ⇒ b = 1

⇒ Substitute b = 1 back into Equation 1:

⇒ a = 5 × 1 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is a = 5, b = 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unique Solution

A system of linear equations has a unique solution if the lines intersect at exactly one point. The condition is a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂.

No Solution

A system of equations has no solution if the lines are parallel and never intersect. The condition is a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂.

Infinitely Many Solutions

A system of equations has infinitely many solutions if the lines overlap entirely, meaning they represent the exact same line. The condition is a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂.
</p
